Had the platform picked Tanimoto as its AD metric, it would have PREDICTED. This vindicates the reviewer's deeper point: without a declared metric, "outside the applicability domain" has no truth value. It also means the platform must report the disagreeing metric, not just the agreeing ones.

3. COMPOSITION ALONE IS SUFFICIENT HERE - AND THE DEMAND FOR AN ERROR CURVE IS UNSATISFIABLE IN THIS SPECIFIC REGION. This is where I part company with the reviewer. An error curve requires labelled molecules at increasing distance from the training distribution. At charge >= +9 there are zero TDC molecules; above 3000 Da there are zero single covalent species. You cannot fit an error-vs-distance curve through a region containing no points, and you cannot honestly extrapolate one there either - that would reproduce the very error the refusal is avoiding. The reviewer's objection is fully valid in the SPARSE regime and invalid in the ZERO regime, and the platform's failure was never having established which regime it was in.

WHY THE OBJECTION "ONE STEP FROM UNFALSIFIABLE" WAS FAIR, AND HOW IT IS ANSWERED. It was fair because nothing about the old rule could be falsified: no acceptance region was ever exhibited, no number was ever produced, and the justification was a general claim about training-set character that no computation could contradict. It is answered not by argument but by three artifacts: (i) counted support (0 of 53,525 at charge >= +9; heaviest single molecule 2285.7 Da); (ii) a numeric margin on this query (h/h* = 120x; kNN 60x threshold); (iii) a published acceptance rate, which converts "can only ever refuse" into a testable proposition. Conformal outlier detection makes (iii) a theorem: P(refuse | in-distribution) <= alpha.

WHAT DOES NOT RESCUE THE PREDICTION. (a) Conformal prediction gives MARGINAL coverage, averaged over the test distribution - it says nothing about one 4943 Da polycation. (b) Object-conditional coverage is provably impossible distribution-free; imposing it yields intervals of infinite length. (c) Mondrian conformal would help only if the bin "MW > 3000, charge >= +9" contained calibration molecules; it contains zero. (d) Covariate-shift conformal needs w(x) = p_test/p_train, undefined at zero training density. (e) Ensemble variance is free here (ADMET-AI already ensembles 5 models per endpoint) but is the least trustworthy signal available: Ovadia et al. measured that "the quality of uncertainty consistently degrades with increasing dataset shift regardless of method", and Hirschfeld et al. - co-authored by an ADMET-AI author - found "no method consistently satisfied the objective of producing a strong ranking of errors". A narrow ensemble SD at 4943 Da would be an artifact, not reassurance.

ONE FURTHER POINT AGAINST THE PLATFORM. The ADMET-AI paper itself declares no applicability domain. I fetched it and found no statement of chemical-space limits, no molecular-weight range, and no limitations section constraining its scope. Under OECD Principle 3 the model as published is therefore incomplete for regulatory use, and the burden of defining the AD falls on the deploying platform - which is this platform. That obligation is met by computing and publishing an AD, not by installing a cutoff.

BOTTOM LINE. Keep the refusal; discard its justification. Replace "MW > 1000 Da, because the training sets contain no large peptides" with a defined, pre-registered, conformal-calibrated AD that reports numbers, publishes its acceptance rate, and names the descriptors that actually fired. The molecule genuinely is outside the domain - by 120x on leverage, 60x on local density, and on an exactly-zero support count for its charge class. It was simply never, until now, shown to be.
applicability_domain.implementation:
CONCRETE IMPLEMENTATION - everything below runs with what is already available: RDKit (2026.03.5, verified), the ADMET-AI 5-model ensemble, and TDC data downloadable from Harvard Dataverse. Working scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-seunghojung-Documents-DeepMind-Bio/a981ed0e-7f93-4115-84a0-d516f5c26372/scratchpad/ (mw2.py, frag.py, tani.py, ad2.py).

STEP 0 - PIN THE REFERENCE SET (this is what makes the AD auditable).
Download TDC datasets directly; no PyTDC install needed:
  curl -sL -o caco2_wang.tsv https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/access/datafile/4259569
Dataset -> dataverse ID mapping lives in the name2id dict at line 964 of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mims-harvard/TDC/main/tdc/metadata.py. IDs verified working this session: caco2_wang 4259569, hia_hou 4259591, pgp_broccatelli 4259597, bioavailability_ma 4259567, lipophilicity_astrazeneca 4259595, solubility_aqsoldb 4259610, bbb_martins 4259566, ppbr_az 6413140, vdss_lombardo 4267387, half_life_obach 4266799, clearance_hepatocyte_az 4266187, ld50_zhu 4267146, herg 4259588, ames 4259564, dili 4259585, cyp3a4_veith 4259582. Files are TSV; the SMILES column is "Drug" in most and "X" in vdss_lombardo, half_life_obach, ld50_zhu, clearance_hepatocyte_az. Extend to all 41 datasets ADMET-AI uses. Record SHA256 and molecule count per file and store them alongside the AD definition - the AD is only meaningful relative to a pinned training set.

STEP 1 - BUILD THE AD PER ENDPOINT, NOT GLOBALLY.
OECD para 98 requires a model-specific AD: "every model should be associated with its own AD derived not only on the chemicals in the training set but also on the descriptors and (statistical) approach used to develop the model." I pooled all 16 datasets for the diagnosis above; production must compute one AD per TDC endpoint, because Caco2 permeability and hERG have different chemical spaces and different reliable regions. Store per endpoint: descriptor means, standard deviations, per-descriptor min/max, the (X^T X)^-1 matrix (or its pseudo-inverse), and the training kNN-distance distribution.

STEP 2 - DESCRIPTOR SPACE.
Use the same 200 RDKit descriptors ADMET-AI already computes (it is a Chemprop-RDKit model: Chemprop "augmented with 200 physicochemical molecular features that are computed by the" RDKit package). Reusing exactly those descriptors means the AD is defined in the model's own feature space, which is the OECD requirement. A transparent 20-descriptor subset (MolWt, HeavyAtoms, MolLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, RotB, Rings, AromRings, FracCsp3, FormalCharge, NumN, NumO, AmideBonds, LabuteASA, BalabanJ, BertzCT, MolMR, NHOHCount, NOCount) reproduced every conclusion in the ruling and is far easier to explain to a reviewer; ship both, lead with the interpretable one. IMPLEMENTATION WARNING I hit: the full RDKit descriptor matrix is rank-deficient, so (X^T X)^-1 does not exist - use numpy.linalg.pinv, or project onto the leading principal components first, and state which you did. Silently inverting a singular matrix is how fake leverage numbers get published.

STEP 3 - THE THREE AD FUNCTIONS, WITH THRESHOLDS FIXED BEFORE THE QUERY.
  (i) Bounding box: reject if any descriptor is outside [min_j, max_j]. Report WHICH descriptors and by how much.
  (ii) Leverage: h = x^T (X^T X)^-1 x on mean-centred standardised descriptors; h* = 3(p+1)/n. Report h, h*, and the ratio. Plot the Williams graph (standardised residual vs h) for the training and test sets so the domain is visible, per OECD para 115.
  (iii) kNN: mean standardised-Euclidean distance to the 5 nearest training molecules; threshold = 95th percentile of the training set's own leave-one-out kNN distances. Declare the percentile in advance.
  (iv) ALSO report nearest-neighbour Tanimoto even though it disagrees. Suppressing the metric that would have permitted the prediction is selective reporting; disclosing it is what makes the panel honest.

STEP 4 - CALIBRATE THE REFUSAL SO IT IS FALSIFIABLE (this is the step that converts case (c) into case (a)).
Use conformal outlier detection (Angelopoulos & Bates eq 14) with the kNN distance as the score s(x):
  s_i = kNN distance of training molecule i (leave-one-out), i = 1..n
  q_hat = numpy.quantile(s, numpy.ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha))/n, method='higher')
  refuse iff s(x_query) > q_hat
With alpha = 0.01 this guarantees P(refuse | molecule drawn from the training distribution) <= 0.01. Publish that number. It is the formal answer to "a platform that can only ever refuse has not been distinguished from a platform that cannot compute": a rule that provably refuses at most 1% of in-distribution molecules is demonstrably not an off-switch. Note this needs only UNLABELLED training molecules - no new experiments.

STEP 5 - PROVE NON-VACUITY EMPIRICALLY.
Run the finished AD over a held-out druglike reference set (e.g. a DrugBank or ChEMBL sample not used to set thresholds) and publish the acceptance rate, plus a worked example of a molecule the platform ACCEPTS with its numbers. Ship this in the same report as any refusal. A refusal accompanied by an acceptance rate is a scientific claim; a refusal alone is a policy.

STEP 6 - CASE (b) MACHINERY, FOR MOLECULES INSIDE BUT FAR FROM CENTRE.
Split the pinned training data ~80/20 into proper-training and calibration (Xu et al. recommend "around 80%" for proper training). Nonconformity alpha_i = |y_i - y_hat_i| / sigma(x_i), with sigma(x) taken from the SD of ADMET-AI's existing 5-model ensemble - free, already computed at inference. Interval: y_hat(x) +/- alpha_theta * sigma(x), with alpha_theta the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n empirical quantile of calibration scores. Then MONDRIANISE: bin molecules by AD score (e.g. leverage deciles), calibrate q_hat separately per bin using q_hat(g) = Quantile(scores in g; ceil((n(g)+1)(1-alpha))/n(g)), and report empirical coverage PER BIN on held-out data, not just marginally. Refuse to create a bin with n(g) below a declared minimum (a few hundred) - a bin with too few calibration points has a guarantee in name only.

STEP 7 - VERIFY THE CONFORMAL IMPLEMENTATION.
Shuffle-and-split the calibration/validation pool R times, recompute empirical coverage each time, and histogram it; the mean must sit at 1-alpha. Angelopoulos & Bates give the analytic check: E[C] = 1 - l/(n+1) with SD sqrt(l(n+1-l)(n+n_val+1) / (n_val * R * (n+1)^2 * (n+2))). If the simulated distribution does not match the observed coverage, the implementation is wrong. Run this before shipping any interval.

STEP 8 - WHAT THE PLATFORM SHOULD ACTUALLY EMIT FOR THIS CANDIDATE.
Not "refused: MW > 1000 Da". Increasing n would NOT fix this, because the defect is not sample size — it is that three of the four auxiliaries were never independently checked. This is Duhem's point exactly, retrieved verbatim: "A physicist can never subject an isolated hypothesis to experimental test, but only a whole group of hypotheses; when the experiment is in disagreement with his predictions, what he learns is that at least one of the hypotheses constituting this group is unacceptable and ought to be modified; but the experiment does not designate which one should be changed."

They are consistent in magnitude and contradictory in sign, and any code path that pipes 8.04 into a dG slot creates a 16 kcal/mol error.

2. THE OUTPUT IS NOT AN IC50. The Boltz-2 authors state they trained "a single affinity value head on all available affinity measurements (eg, Ki, Kd, IC50, AC50, EC50, and XC50)," and justify the pooling by noting that "when comparing affinity values within the same assay, the pairwise differences loss effectively cancel out the correction term." Cross-assay ABSOLUTE values are the one regime where, by the authors' own reasoning, the Cheng-Prusoff correction does not cancel. Comparing this output to a specific measured IC50 is a category mismatch before any noise question arises.

3. THE COMPARISON IS OFF-LABEL. affinity_probability_binary = 0.4447 — the model's own head says non-binder — while the documentation states affinity_pred_value "should only be used when comparing different active molecules, not inactives." The project computed an error metric on a value whose documented usage precondition is false.

And there is a real measurement in the file that everyone missed. affinity_pred_value is the exact arithmetic mean of two ensemble members (verified bit-identical: (-0.25931 + 0.46963)/2 = 0.10515692830085754). Those members disagree by 0.729 log10 units — a 5.4-fold range in IC50, 0.99 kcal/mol — on the identical input. Their binary heads straddle the decision boundary, 0.552 versus 0.337: the ensemble cannot agree on whether the ligand binds at all. That spread is a REFERENCE-FREE, ASSUMPTION-LIGHT DISPERSION MEASUREMENT. It needs no ChEMBL record, no assay-noise correction, no auxiliary hypotheses. It alone accounts for 30% of the headline gap, and it is worth more to this project than the comparison that produced the gap.

Finally, the observation is not reproducible from the archive. Every candidate-fold run in runs/manifest.json preserved an input.yaml; runs/919fef2194e3 did not. The exact submitted SMILES and sequence are gone. I partially recovered them from the mmCIF — chain A has exactly 583 residues, chain B has exactly 18 heavy atoms of composition C15N2O, the correct formula for huperzine A — which is reassuring given that the project's own data/validation_gate.json flags this compound's stored SMILES as unparseable. But formula does not fix stereochemistry, and huperzine A is chiral. For a project whose stated purpose is removing numbers written down without a source, a headline number whose input was not archived is the defect it exists to prevent.

Bottom line: this is a SMOKE TEST that fired, plus an internal dispersion measurement. A smoke test that fires is genuinely informative — it caught a live sign/units contradiction and an out-of-domain usage. It is not a validation, not a calibration, and not an error bar. Retiring it discards three deductive findings and the only dispersion estimate the project owns; keeping it as "validation against ground truth at confidence 0.95" asserts something the data cannot support and that the retrieved base rates actively contradict. Re-type the object; do not delete it.

verification.ruling_upheld:
UPHOLD, with the corrections listed. I re-derived every equation and re-fetched every source rather than auditing the prose, and the ruling's scientific core is sound.

ON THE POINT I WAS TOLD TO PRESS HARDEST — THE TRAINING LABEL. There is no fatal gap. The reviewer did not assert pooling; they retrieved it, and the quotes are exact. I confirmed them independently from the Europe PMC JATS full text (PPR1039145) and the bioRxiv v1 full-text HTML: (a) label construction — "For the binding affinity regression values (e.g., Ki, Kd, IC50, AC50, EC50, XC50), we gather data from PubChem, ChEMBL, and BindingDB… All affinity values are standardized to log 10 scale derived from values measured in µM"; (b) pooling — "We observed best performance when training a single affinity value head on all available affinity measurements… Although these metrics reflect different underlying biochemical quantities, Kis and IC50s are related through the Cheng–Prusoff equation, and when comparing affinity values within the same assay, the pairwise differences loss effectively cancel out the correction term, and assays can be combined Ross et al. [2023]"; (c) loss — "Huber loss applied to both absolute affinity values and, with stronger weight, to the pairwise intra-assay differences"; (d) the appendix curation filter, verbatim as quoted: "Filter to affinity measurements with standard type in {'Ki', 'Kd', 'IC50', 'XC50', 'EC50', 'AC50'}." The centered-metric protocol and the Limitations pocket sentence are also exact. Six referents on one axis is established fact, not inference.

THE CENTRAL RULING IS CORRECT AND I CONFIRM IT INDEPENDENTLY. Term by term: ΔG° = −RT ln K° with K° = Ka·c° = c°/Kd gives ΔG° = +RT ln(Kd/c°). pIC50 = −log10(IC50/M) = 6 − y for y = log10(IC50/µM), so the docs' (6−y)·RT·ln10 = −RT·ln(IC50_M) = −ΔG° under the counterfactual IC50→Kd. Sign-inverted, exactly as the ruling says, and the ruling's |ΔG| discriminator is sharp: for IC50 > 1 M the docs' expression goes negative while |ΔG| cannot. The RT ln K° relation has a precondition — the argument must be a standard equilibrium constant — and a pooled Ki/Kd/IC50/EC50/AC50/XC50 log-potency is not one. The identifiability argument is right: the endpoint type, [S], Km and mechanism are discarded at label-construction time, so no function of the output alone recovers ΔG°. I verified every number: RT(298.15 K) = 0.592485, RT·ln10 = 1.364247 (so 1.364 is correct to 4 s.f. and reproduces thermo.py's RT = 1.987204259e-3 × 298.15 exactly); RT·ln2 = 0.410679; 3·RT·ln10 = 4.092741; factors 2/4/11 → 0.3010/0.6021/1.0414 log10 → 0.4107/0.8214/1.4207 kcal/mol; Kd 1 nM/5 nM/1274 nM → −12.278/−11.325/−8.042. Cheng–Prusoff verified in both published forms from three independent open-access sources: "KI = IC50/(1 + ([S]/KM))" (PMC11790956) and "Ki = IC50/[1 + ([L]/Kd)], where [L] and Kd are the concentration and binding affinity of the radiolabeled ligand in the assay" (PMC11915030). All three IUPAC Gold Book entries, all seven IUPHAR/BPS definitions, both Cer et al. quotes, all three Ross et al. quotes (including Kramer's 0.56 pKi/0.77 kcal and 0.69 pKi/0.95 kcal), and all four ChEMBL FAQ quotes are verbatim as given. The run data check out to the last bit: affinity_pred_value == (−0.2593143582344055 + 0.4696282148361206)/2 exactly, spread 0.72894 log10 = 0.9945 kcal/mol, probability 0.44470 from members 0.55217/0.33722, iptm 0.7136427, msa=empty per the frozen prespec. And I confirmed by reading platform/cbc/thermo.py that check() guards with `if dg < tightest` against −18.3, so a positive +8.04 can never trigger it — the guard is dead exactly as claimed. Wan, Zhang, Xue & Coveney (arXiv:2603.05532) is real, correctly attributed, the compound counts (16,780 / 21,702) are right, and the concluding sentences are verbatim.

WHERE I WOULD STRENGTHEN THE RULING — four retrieved items it missed, all of which support it. (1) The single most on-point authorial statement is in the Affinity module section and is not cited anywhere in the ruling: "the predicted value should be viewed as a general measure of binding strength that supports ranking and can be approximately interpreted as an IC50-like value." The authors themselves say ranking and IC50-like. This should lead the evidence, ahead of the inferential arguments. (2) The corpus was deliberately built to teach differences rather than levels: "Assays with insufficient data or a low affinity standard deviation are discarded to encourage learning of intra-assay differences in values rather than inter-assay." (3) The sentence immediately following the centered-metric quote makes the authors' intent explicit: "This adjustment allows for a fair comparison with methods that only predict relative affinities, such as relative FEP." (4) A gap the platform will otherwise trip over: the appendix states "All predictions are converted to kcal/mol prior to computing the metrics." The authors DO express this head's output in kcal/mol. The ruling's claim that the paper never calls it a binding free energy is true — I checked all 19 occurrences of "free energy" in the full text and every one refers to FEP/ABFE/MM-PBSA methods or to the external ΔG reference, never to the head's output — but the ruling should say plainly that kcal/mol UNITS are the authors' own usage for a log-potency, and that the prohibition attaches to the NAME (ΔG, free energy, Kd) and to the sign, not to the unit. Left unstated, someone will find that appendix line and conclude the panel was uninformed.

The three extensions (a)-(c) are correct and should be adopted: the Kd/Ka/Ki/pKd/pKi family is the same defect one level down and currently passes the build check; the re-ranking to pooled-referent-first is right because sign is the only reparable defect and leading with it invites the false repair; and the absolute-value prohibition should indeed extend to reporting a bare predicted IC50. The refusal of the "apparent/effective ΔG" carve-out is also right, and for the reason given — that convention presumes a single-referent Kd/Ki training target, which this head does not have.

The two are not the same quantity. Measured this session: the ruling's own proxy peptide returns Chem.GetFormalCharge = 0, i.e. on the training set's own scale the query is neutral and sits inside the training FormalCharge range [-30, +5]; FormalCharge is correspondingly absent from the 7 bounding-box descriptors that fired. On a protonation-state-independent measure (basic centres: aliphatic amine + guanidine SMARTS over 42,343 unique training molecules) 216 molecules have >= 4 basic centres and 5 have >= 9. The charge axis is therefore SPARSE-BUT-NONZERO, which by the ruling's own dichotomy mandates a measured error curve rather than composition alone. The zero-support conclusion survives only on the molecular-weight axis (heaviest single covalent fragment 2285.7 Da, verified).

errors.item: C2: conformal outlier detection "converts C2 from a courtesy into a theorem" and is "the formal answer" to the off-switch objection
errors.claimed: Angelopoulos & Bates eq (14), P(C(X_test)=outlier) <= alpha, proves the platform refuses at most 1% of in-distribution molecules and therefore is demonstrably not an off-switch.
errors.actual: Eq (14) and Proposition 3 verified verbatim, but they guarantee only false-positive control on the clean-data distribution and hold for ANY score function - including a constant or random one - because q_hat is defined as the (1-alpha) quantile of the training scores. The source states this limitation directly: "As with standard conformal prediction, the score function is very important for the method to perform well-that is, to be effective at flagging outliers." The bound is satisfied by construction, says nothing about power, and says nothing about the distribution of molecules users actually submit: a platform refusing 100% of real queries satisfies eq (14) exactly. The non-vacuity claim rests entirely on the empirical held-out acceptance rate (Step 5), not on the theorem.

errors.claimed: One membership function and one threshold, pre-registered, decide the case.
errors.actual: The ruling then runs a four-metric panel (bounding box, leverage, kNN, Tanimoto) and never declares an aggregation rule - the same defect it correctly identifies in the platform ("without a declared metric, 'outside the applicability domain' has no truth value"). The verdict for this molecule flips with the rule: reject-if-ANY refuses it, reject-if-ALL accepts it, because Tanimoto (0.595, verified) does not flag it. Measured this session on the 2,845-molecule DrugBank reference set that ships with ADMET-AI: reject-if-ANY refuses 18.98% (bounding box 0.49%, leverage 13.29%, kNN 14.06%).

errors.claimed: Implementable with what the project has, and expected to demonstrate a high acceptance rate.
errors.actual: Not implementable as specified with the assets present. The only reference set in the project (drugbank.csv, 2,845 parsed molecules) has 56.2% exact-canonical-SMILES overlap with the pooled TDC training data measured this session, so it is not held out. Running the ruling's own rules on it gives 81.02% acceptance under reject-if-ANY, not ~96%; leverage alone refuses 13.29% of approved drugs versus 3.30% of the training set. The acceptance-rate demonstration must therefore be built on a genuinely disjoint set, and the panel's aggregation retuned, before it can support the non-vacuity argument.

errors.item: Reference set integrity: n = 53,525 treated as the calibration population for leverage, the kNN percentile threshold, and conformal outlier detection
errors.claimed: 53,525 valid molecules pooled from 16 TDC datasets, kNN threshold = 95th percentile of the training leave-one-out distribution = 1.623, h* = 3(p+1)/53525.
errors.actual: The molecule count reproduces exactly, but 11,182 of the 53,525 rows (20.9%) are duplicate canonical SMILES (42,343 unique; 6,289 molecules appear >= 2 times), because the 16 datasets share compounds. Measured consequences: 39.3% of training molecules have a zero-distance neighbour among their 5 nearest, so the LOO kNN distribution is deflated - deduplicating raises the 95th-percentile threshold from 1.623 to 1.880 and drops the candidate's margin from 60.3x to 52.1x; and on unique molecules h* = 0.001488, dropping the leverage margin from 120x to 95x. More seriously, duplicates break the exchangeability premise of Theorem D.1 and Proposition 3 outright, so the eq (14) false-refusal bound does not hold on this corpus as assembled. Pooling 16 heterogeneous assay datasets is also not an i.i.d. draw from any single distribution.

errors.item: Feature space and model specificity of the advertised AD numbers (Step 8 emit block)
errors.claimed: h = 0.1417 vs h* = 0.001177 (120x), kNN 60x, 7 of 20 descriptors outside - offered as the AD of the deployed ADMET-AI model.
errors.actual: All figures reproduce exactly, but they are computed in a 20-descriptor RDKit space with a linear hat matrix, while ADMET-AI is a Chemprop message-passing GNN using 200 RDKit features plus learned graph embeddings, and all figures are pooled across 16 endpoints. verification.ruling_upheld:
UPHOLD WITH CORRECTIONS. The outcome is right, the source discipline is unusually good, and the reproducibility is excellent - but four load-bearing pillars of the argument are weaker than stated, and one of them (the charge-axis "counted zero") is measuring the wrong quantity.

WHAT SURVIVED RE-CHECK, IN FULL. Every verbatim quotation I could test is accurate. OECD ENV/JM/MONO(2007)2 paras 98, 100, 108-116 check word-for-word against the PDF I fetched independently (oecd.org content/dam .../9789264085442-en.pdf, 154 pp). The leverage threshold is exactly as quoted: para 112 reads "A 'warning leverage' (h*) is generally fixed at 3p/n, where n is the number of training chemicals, and p the number of descriptors plus one" - and the submission's reconciliation with the h* = 3(p+1)/n form is algebraically correct. The hat-matrix equation is transcribed exactly from Khurshid et al. arXiv:2411.00920 s2.0.2, stray closing parenthesis and all; so are eqs (1), (3) and (4), including the printed missing square in the standard-deviation formula, which the submission flagged rather than silently repaired - the right call. Angelopoulos & Bates arXiv:2107.07511v6 eq (1), the marginal-coverage definition, the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n quantile, Theorem D.1, eqs (8)-(9) with Propositions 1-2, s4.4 eq (14) with Proposition 3, the likelihood ratio w(x) = dP_test/dP, and Theorem 3 with "a somewhat restricted case-that of a known covariate shift" all verify. Fontana/Zeni/Vantini arXiv:2005.07972 eqs (3.2), (3.3), (3.7), the Mondrian taxonomy passage and the infinite-length consequence verify. Xu et al. arXiv:2304.00970 eq (1), the interval y_hat +/- alpha_theta*sigma, "Marginal, is roughly understood as averaged over all molecules", "usually impossible to achieve", and the ~80% proper-training split verify. Ovadia and Hirschfeld verify, and Kyle Swanson is indeed an author of the latter and of ADMET-AI. Sheridan 2004, Sheridan 2015 and Mora 2024 verify verbatim against PubMed. All 16 Harvard Dataverse IDs are correct, and name2id is at line 964 of tdc/metadata.py exactly as claimed.

I also re-ran the chemistry from scratch on freshly downloaded files. Every number reproduces to the digit: 53,525 molecules; MW median 305.3 / p90 478.6 / p99 781.7 / p99.9 1450.3 / p99.99 2285.7 / max 5299.5; 224 (0.42%) > 1000 Da, 11 > 2000, 1 > 3000; the single >3000 entry is a multi-component ester mixture and the heaviest single covalent fragment in the corpus is 2285.7 Da; 97.19% neutral, max +5 on one molecule; the same 7 of 20 descriptors outside the bounding box (TPSA, HBD, RotB, NumN, AmideBonds, NHOHCount, NOCount) with MolWt inside; h = 0.1417, h* = 0.001177, 120x; kNN 97.91 vs p95 1.623 (60.3x) and vs training max 73.58 (1.33x); Tanimoto 0.595 with 23.6% of training molecules more isolated. That is an unusually clean audit.

ON CONFORMAL PREDICTION, PRECISELY. It guarantees marginal coverage, 1-alpha <= P(Y_test in C(X_test)) <= 1-alpha+1/(n+1), under i.i.d. or exchangeability, with the probability averaged over both the calibration draw and the test draw, for any model and any distribution. It does NOT guarantee: coverage for a named molecule (object-conditional coverage is impossible distribution-free - Fontana eq 3.2 via Lei & Wasserman Lemma 1 - and imposing it forces infinite-length intervals); coverage in any subgroup unless you calibrate per group with n(g) > 0; validity under shift unless the density ratio is known (Theorem 3), which is undefined where training density is zero; that the point prediction is any good; or, for the outlier variant, any ability to detect real outliers. The submission states all of this correctly and it is the strongest part of the document - with one exception, which is where it overclaims: eq (14) is not the answer to the off-switch objection. It holds for any score function whatsoever, is satisfied by construction, and constrains only refusal on the training distribution. A platform that refuses every molecule a user actually submits satisfies it exactly. Only the measured held-out acceptance rate answers the reviewer, and the theorem should be demoted to what it is - a calibration device, not a proof of usefulness.

DOES THE CRITERION SEPARATE PRINCIPLED REFUSAL FROM EVASION? Mostly yes, and it is a large improvement on "MW > 1000 Da". C3 and C4 are excellent: demanding a number and demanding that the stated ground be the computed ground would kill the original justification on its own, and the finding that MW 4910 Da sits inside the training MW envelope while hydrogen-bonding and amide-count descriptors are what actually fire is the single most valuable result in the document. But C1 and C2 have holes that let an evasion back in. C1 specifies one function and one threshold while the analysis runs a four-metric panel with no declared aggregation rule - and the verdict for this very molecule flips between the two obvious rules, since Tanimoto passes it. That is the ruling's own argument turned on the ruling. C2's acceptance-rate test is the right idea but, measured on the only reference set the project has, the ruling's rules accept 81%, not the ~96% it floats, and refuse 13% of approved drugs on leverage alone. A criterion that refuses one in five marketed drugs will not be accepted by a regulator as a demonstration of non-vacuity; it will be read as evidence the domain is drawn too tight.

WOULD A REGULATOR ACCEPT IT? Not in its current form, for three reasons that are all fixable. First, OECD Principle 3 as the ruling itself quotes it requires the AD to be defined on the model's own descriptors and per model; the advertised numbers come from a 20-descriptor linear hat matrix pooled over 16 endpoints, applied to a message-passing GNN. Second, the reference corpus is 20.9% duplicated, which deflates the kNN threshold, inflates the leverage denominator, and breaks the exchangeability premise every conformal guarantee in the document rests on. Third, the charge-axis zero is a unit error, and it matters because it is one of two legs holding up the "composition alone suffices" dichotomy.

IS IT IMPLEMENTABLE WITH WHAT THIS PROJECT HAS? Substantially yes - better than I expected. RDKit 2026.03.5, admet_ai 2.0.1, chemprop 2.3.1, torch 2.13.0 and scipy are all installed and working; the TDC files download reliably; the whole panel runs in minutes. Steps 0-4 are immediately executable. Step 5 is not, as written, because the only reference set present overlaps the training data by 56.2%. Step 6 (Mondrian split conformal on labelled data) is executable per endpoint since the TDC labels are in the same files. Step 7 is executable.

WHERE I PART FROM THE RULING ON SUBSTANCE. The dichotomy "zero support => composition suffices; sparse support => error curve mandatory" is the right frame and I endorse it. But the ruling placed this case in the zero bucket on two axes and only one of them holds. Above ~2300 Da the zero is real, counted, and robust to how you draw the molecule. At "charge >= +9" the zero is an artifact of comparing the candidate's physiological charge against the training set's as-drawn formal charges - on which the ruling's own proxy peptide also scores zero. Measured protonation-independently, 216 unique training molecules carry four or more basic centres and five carry nine or more. So the charge axis is sparse, not empty, and by the ruling's own standard it demands a binned error curve. Drop the charge argument, or re-run it on a pH-7.4 protonation model, and rest the refusal where it is unassailable: no single covalent species above 2285.7 Da, the query at 2.16x that, seven size- and polarity-extensive descriptors outside the envelope, and a local density 52-60x beyond the pre-registered threshold depending on deduplication. That is more than enough, and it is honest.

WHAT TO CHANGE, CONCRETELY. (1) Deduplicate on canonical SMILES before computing any threshold, and report n_unique alongside n. (2) Declare the aggregation rule for the panel in advance and justify it against the measured acceptance rate; reject-if-ANY at these thresholds is too aggressive to defend. (3) Build the acceptance-rate set by removing the 56.2% of DrugBank that is already in TDC, then publish the rate on the remainder. (4) Recompute the AD per endpoint in ADMET-AI's own 200-feature space and state the rank and the pseudo-inverse explicitly - the 20-descriptor matrix is rank 19, which the implementation notes did not disclose. (5) Replace the charge claim with either a pH-7.4 charge model or a basic-centre count, and report the non-zero counts honestly. (6) Demote eq (14) from proof-of-non-vacuity to calibration device. Do those six things and the refusal is defensible in a regulatory submission. Until then it is a correct decision resting on two sound legs, one broken one, and a theorem that has been asked to carry a claim it cannot bear.

The record is in /Users/seunghojung/Documents/DeepMind_Bio/data/corpus_ACHE.json: HUPERZINE A, CHEMBL395280, {"activity_type": "IC50", "value_nm": 5.0, "assay_confidence": null, "assay_chembl_id": "CHEMBL643374", "document": "CHEMBL1129143"}. platform/cbc/corpus.py:214 populates activity_type from `a.get("standard_type") or ""`, so standard_type was present and equal to "IC50". The field that is null is assay_confidence (ChEMBL's target-assignment confidence score) — a different field with a different meaning. grep for standard_type across data/ and platform/ returns only corpus.py:199 and :214; no null standard_type exists anywhere in the repo. This is the load-bearing empirical premise of the ruling's central argument (that the reference, not the model, is the probable defect), it is repeated four times, and the ruling instructs that it be written verbatim into the ledger — which would inject exactly the class of unsourced number the project exists to remove.

errors.item: Inference #8 — transfer of the Kalliokoski Table 2 base rate to odds on the reference record
errors.claimed: "8 out of 10 sampled pairs ... were found to be INVALID ... giving prior odds of roughly 4:1 that the REFERENCE is the defective element" and "The most probable single explanation for this discrepancy is a bad reference record, not a bad model."
errors.actual: Table 2 is verbatim-correct (verified in Europe PMC PMC3628986: ΔpIC50 2.5 → "8" invalid out of 10, error types "unit error, receptor subtype error, value error"; 3.2 → 10; 1.5 → "6 (+2 dubious)"). But a Kalliokoski "pair" is TWO independent literature measurements, so 8/10 estimates P(at least one of the two records is erroneous | Δ≈2.5) = 0.8. It does not give 4:1 on a designated member: absent further information the per-record rate is roughly 0.4–0.5, i.e. odds near 1:1, not 4:1. Worse, the second member of the project's pair is not a literature record at all but a model output with its own large, unconstrained error scale, so the pair-level rate cannot be transferred without assuming the model is as reliable as a curated record — the very thing at issue. Calling the result "prior odds" is also loose (it is a conditional-on-Δ posterior-type quantity). The qualitative direction — record error is a live and common explanation at this Δ — survives; the quantified 4:1 and "most probable single explanation" do not.

The inference is labelled "deductive" and "auxiliary-free in the Duhem-Quine sense" while resting on a false statement about what the platform does.

errors.item: Inference #2 — strength label "deductive" for ¬U2 (affinity_pred_value is NOT an estimate of IC50)
errors.claimed: "affinity_pred_value is NOT an estimate of IC50, so calling the 2.41-log gap a prediction error against a measured IC50 is a category mismatch." Strength: deductive.
errors.actual: The two quotes cited are verbatim-correct (verified in PMC12262699 fullTextXML). But the ruling omits the sentence in the same paper that bears most directly on the question, from the Affinity module section: "As such, the predicted value should be viewed as a general measure of binding strength that supports ranking and can be approximately interpreted as an IC50-like value." The authors explicitly license approximate IC50 interpretation of the absolute value. That does not rescue the project's use of it, but it defeats "deductive" and "category mismatch": the correct strength is at most strong, and the correct claim is that the absolute value is uncalibrated across assays, not that it is not an IC50 estimate at all.

errors.item: Inference #6 — y = 0 as the model's no-information point / prior mean
errors.claimed: "y = 0 corresponds to IC50 = 1 μM, the exact centre of the model's log10(μM) output scale" ... "statistically indistinguishable from a null/shrunk-to-mean output" ... assumption "that the training distribution is centred near 1 μM, which the docs' own calibration examples (-3 strong / 0 moderate / +2 weak) imply."
errors.actual: NOT RETRIEVED and not implied. The docs' three examples (-3, 0, +2) are verbatim-correct but are asymmetric about 0 (midpoint -0.5) and are labelled strong/moderate/weak — a calibration illustration, not a distribution. Nothing in docs/prediction.md or in PMC12262699 states the mean, median or centre of the affinity training-label distribution; searches of the full text for "distribution of affinity" and related terms return zero hits. Since y=0 being the training mean is the sole premise for "the gap measures distance to the model's prior mean" and for "the SIGN of the discrepancy carries no information", both conclusions (repeated in unlicensed_inferences item 9 and in the closing paragraph of how_to_use_it_here) are unsupported. Regression to the mean is a real hazard here, but its magnitude and even its direction are unestimated.

errors.item: Inference #4 — treating value1/value2 as an n=2 replicate and applying the range estimator of scale
errors.claimed: "a genuine n=2 replicate measurement" / "reference-free, assumption-free measurement of the method's own dispersion" / "Two-replicate sd estimator |x1-x2|/sqrt(2) = 0.5154 log10 units" (written into proposed ledger claim clm_NEW_ensemble at confidence 0.85)
errors.actual: The numbers are exact (verified: mean identity bit-identical for both value and binary heads; |v2-v1| = 0.7289425730705261; /√2 = 0.51544; 10^0.7289 = 5.357-fold; 0.5504 μM vs 2.9487 μM; 30.29% of the gap). But docs/prediction.md lines 233-236 describe value1/value2 as "the first model of the ensemble" and "the second model of the ensemble" — two fixed trained models, deterministic given the input, not two i.i.d. draws from a noise distribution. The d2 = √2 range estimator requires i.i.d. normal replicates; between-model disagreement of a two-member ensemble does not satisfy that, and correlated members bias the estimate downward. The quantity 0.7289 is a valid, useful measurement of ensemble disagreement; "assumption-free", "replicate", and "sd estimator" are all overstated, and the ruling's own stated support (the mean identity) establishes aggregation, not independence. Separately, the docs' own example JSON has affinity_pred_value 0.8367 with value1 = value2 = 0.8225, contradicting the mean identity — so the identity is an empirical property of this file, not a documented one.

errors.item: Inference #10 — Jeffreys-prior posterior summaries, and their reuse in unlicensed_inferences item 4
errors.claimed: "(a) Jeffreys p(σ)∝1/σ: posterior median 2.58, 95% CrI [0.35, 10.38], P(σ>1) 0.350 -> 0.888, BF 14.75" and, as a standalone conclusion, "under the reference prior the posterior on σ² is Inverse-Gamma(1/2, d²/2), whose mean is infinite and whose 95% credible interval spans [0.35, 10.38] log units."
errors.actual: I reproduced every figure exactly — but only by guessing the grid, which turns out to be log-uniform σ ∈ [0.01, 12]. The prior P(σ>1) = 0.350 is a pure artifact of that truncation (an improper 1/σ prior assigns no such probability), and the BF is computed as posterior-odds/prior-odds against it, so BF 14.75 is equally an artifact. Re-running on other defensible grids: [0.001,100] → CrI [0.16, 40.56], BF 12.44; [0.05,5] → CrI [0.41, 4.74], BF 12.20; [0.01,50] → CrI [0.40, 29.19], BF 10.67. The quoted upper limit 10.38 is 87% of the grid ceiling — it is measuring the grid, not the data. None of this is disclosed. The ruling's own sensitivity statement ("the BAYES FACTOR is stable at 3.1-5.5 across all proper priors") is correct and is the honest result; but it then quotes the improper-prior CrI as a substantive finding in the unlicensed_inferences section, which is the same overreach it is criticising. Minor related point: Inv-Gamma(1/2, d²/2) is the posterior for the TOTAL variance τ² = σ_m² + σ_a², not for σ_m². The "infinite posterior mean" conclusion (shape 1/2 < 1) is nevertheless correct.

## 1. THE AFFINITY-HEAD NAMING RULING

### What the output is

**`affinity_pred_value` is a single scalar on a learned log₁₀(µM) potency axis, fitted jointly to pooled Ki/Kd/IC50/AC50/EC50/XC50 labels under a loss weighted toward within-assay pairwise differences; its ordering is the quantity the training objective optimised, and its absolute level is an uncalibrated corpus-average offset.**

That is the sentence a scientist will accept, and it is the sentence the Boltz-2 authors themselves come closest to writing: *"the predicted value should be viewed as a general measure of binding strength that supports ranking and can be approximately interpreted as an IC50-like value."*

I take that authorial sentence — surfaced by Verifier 1, missed by the specialist — as decisive on one sub-point and on one only. It defeats the specialist's claim that calling the output an IC50 estimate is a *category mismatch* established *deductively*. The authors explicitly license approximate IC50-like reading. **The correct claim is weaker and still sufficient: the absolute level is uncalibrated across assays, and the authors say "ranking" and "approximately."** Downgrade that inference from `deductive` to `strong`. Nothing else changes.

### Is the dG prohibition upheld?

**UPHELD, and EXTENDED.** No carve-out. Three independent grounds, re-ranked as the specialist correctly urged:

1. **Pooled referent (fatal, irreparable).** Six endpoint types on one axis. The information needed to recover ΔG° — endpoint type, [S], Km, mechanism — was destroyed at label-construction time. This is an identifiability failure, not a calibration deficit. No constant inverts a many-to-one map.
2. **IC50 ≠ Kd (systematic, quantified).** At the most benign condition, [S] = Km competitive, IC50/Ki = 2 exactly → 0.4107 kcal/mol of one-signed bias, which already consumes over half the 0.77 kcal/mol public-data reproducibility floor.
3. **Sign (real, one-character, and the trap).** (6−y)·1.364 = **+8.0406**; `thermo.kd_to_dg(1.2740e-6)` = **−8.0420**. Same magnitude, opposite sign. The residual is **0.00146 kcal/mol**, not the 0.001 the specialist stated (Verifier 1 correct), and is entirely the docs' rounding of RT·ln10 = 1.364247 to 1.364.

### "Apparent" / "effective" ΔG — REFUSED

The docking-literature carve-out presumes a **single-referent** Kd/Ki regression target. This head has six referents. "Apparent ΔG" widens an error bar; the defect here is identity, and it is sign-inverted besides. A caveated "apparent ΔG = +8.04" is not a hedged claim, it is a wrong claim about the direction of a thermodynamic driving force. **There is no permissible qualified form. Do not ship one.**

### On kcal/mol as a unit — I rule against both the specialist and the paper

Verifier 1 correctly flags that the Boltz-2 appendix states *"All predictions are converted to kcal/mol prior to computing the metrics."* The authors do express this head's output in kcal/mol. The specialist's claim that the paper never calls it a binding free energy survives (19 occurrences of "free energy", all referring to FEP/ABFE/MM-PBSA or to the external ΔG reference).

But Verifier 3 caught the specialists in a self-contradiction that decides the matter: the n=1 ruling condemns "3.3 kcal/mol" for dressing a pooled-endpoint score in thermodynamic units, then renders the ensemble spread as "0.99 kcal/mol" in the replacement ledger claim it wants written. A *difference* of pooled log-potencies is no more a ΔΔG than an absolute value is a ΔG.

**Ruling: this platform renders nothing from this head in kcal/mol — not the value, not the difference, not the ensemble spread.** log₁₀ units only. The unit costs nothing to drop and is the single thing that invites the mislabel. Record in the ledger that the authors do use kcal/mol, and that the platform declines to, so that nobody later "discovers" the appendix line and concludes the panel was uninformed.

**No. Delete it.** It fails on its own terms, and the specialist's measurement is what kills it: MW 4910 Da is **inside** the training MW bounding box (training max 5299.5 Da).
